P1.evidence: No setter code and no application, so the read-back does not apply. Unusually for this rep, the frame was omitted entirely — not even the three-part version he uses everywhere else. After a time check ('Do you have the full like 40 minutes?') he went straight to 'let's dive into it. Firstly, where did you come across us?' No expectations set, no agreement sought. The opening question was the source-and-resonance variant rather than the scripted open: 'When you saw Trevor, saw Kettlebell Body, what spoke to you and resonated with you specifically?'

P2.evidence: One of only two calls in this folder where the rep announced and ran the block: 'All right, man. Let's get a bit of a baseline for yourself. How old are you?' Age, height and weight all captured — 32, 6'2", 190-195. The training week is the most complete in the batch, elicited properly with 'Monday to Sunday, what does the schedule look like for yourself? Exercise-wise' and producing a full nine-to-ten-session breakdown. Results from current training were pursued well through the plateau line of questioning: 'How long would you say you've plateaued for?' Work was asked but late and without the desk-bound sub-question. The gaps are health, injuries, diet, sleep and energy — none asked. Diet is the notable one: nutrition is pillar two, the prospect named 'having a better quality meal routine' as a benefit he wanted, and he was never asked what he currently eats. Health and injury questions are absent again, though nothing was disclosed and this is a healthy 32-year-old, so the risk here is low.

P3.evidence: Excellent, and the deepest identity work in the folder alongside the Andrew Freeman call. The bridge was asked directly and twice — 'I hear next level a lot. Like, why do you want to go to the next level, Kyle?' and then 'would you say that you are 100% living up to your full potential now?' The ripple sequence ran — 'how do you see this rippling into the different areas of your life?' — and the who-else move produced the richest material on the call: 'How do you see that playing out in your interaction with those that you love?' That opened bloodline, family name, elders, faith and procreation. The rep then went one level further than anywhere else in this batch with two genuinely good follow-ups: 'Do you feel the burden within your family to be that guy to kind of inspire everyone?' and 'are you the oldest?' The reflect-back closed it properly: 'that's the top of the mountain that we aspire to get you to. Most people think, Kyle, this is just about swinging a few kettlebells... It's about helping you to step into a higher identity of yourself.' Only the surface checks are short — the one-thing-you'd-change and can't-do-yet questions were never asked in scripted form.

P4.evidence: Complete and the cleanest run of this phase in the folder. The self-sufficiency challenge was delivered almost verbatim: 'Create your own structure, ChatGPT, YouTube, Claude, this information is so abundant in 2026. Why haven't you done that in the last, I don't know, two years?' It produced a substantive answer rather than a concession — the prospect described the apps and modular programmes he had bought, why they failed ('a lot of it's kind of just contained all the same movements and things that I've already done previously'), and the real limitation ('if you don't have the contextual information, it's hard to actually get the right answers out of the AI'). The rep then gave him credit rather than pressing — 'You don't strike me as someone who's just about BS-ing and giving themselves excuses' — and closed the phase with the correct question: 'what do you feel like needs to be different?' The prospect named the gap himself: 'having a system, a structure and a roadmap that I can hold myself accountable to.'

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was built. There is no two-year question, no cost of inaction, no why-not and no line in the sand. The rep did make one good diagnostic challenge at 00:17:57 — 'Would you like me to be honest or nice in this moment?' followed by 'it seems you've plateaued because you're in good shape. You're fine with kind of where you are health-wise. There's nothing specifically tangibly wrong with you. Hence, there's no drive or need to actually get to the next level' — which is a settle-for challenge in substance and drew a thoughtful answer about discipline versus motivation. But he then asked a question that gave the pain away rather than building it: 'do you feel like there needs to be a catalyst or fire for you to jump to the next level?' and pre-conceded 'we're not going to put that fire inside of you.' Against a prospect who is comfortable by his own description, the Consequence Frame was the entire job, and it did not run.

P6.evidence: The trust gauge ran and returned a six or seven, the second-lowest in the batch, and the rep probed it well — 'Why am I not hearing the nine or 10, dude?' — surfacing exactly the right blocker: 'limitations of time, involvement, touch points... I just haven't really seen a ton of content or information.' That is a clear, specific, solvable objection and the script says a six or seven routes back to Phase 5. Instead the rep asked a softer confirmation ('can you see yourself actually committing to three to four times a week?'), got a yes to a different question, and presented price. The all-in question was never asked. Everything that went wrong in the following ten minutes was named by the prospect at 00:29:49 and left unaddressed.

P11.evidence: The rep disqualified the prospect from the coaching programme, so payment, the Trevor booking, the agreement and the coaching onboarding sequence were all unreachable. Worth crediting separately: he applied the same discipline to the lower-tier product that P11 asks for on the main one — put the link in chat, waited on the call while the account was created, and verified access before signing off ('Can you confirm you can see the classroom, can see the community' — 'All right, brother. You're in'). That is the behaviour the phase is trying to instil, applied to a $200 subscription.

objection_plays.detail: SCRIPT GAP AND THE REASON THIS CALL DID NOT CLOSE — the buyer who wants one part of the bundle. Stated with unusual precision: 'transparently, I thought I was getting a program, like a workout program and a nutrition plan. I didn't know I was signing up for a coaching program and working the one-on-one and altering my mindset and all these other things.' He is not sceptical of coaching, he sells coaching — 'I run a coaching program myself. I'm familiar with all of this.' He simply did not want that component. There is no scripted play for defending a bundle to a buyer who has credibly self-served part of it, and no unbundled tier between $200/mo and $4,000. Second occurrence in this batch after Hamdi Hmimy, and in both cases it was the deciding objection. This should be treated as a product and script build, not a rep coaching point.

SCRIPT GAP — the documentation request. 'Does he have a landing page or anything like that that includes some more information?' plus 'assuming there's case studies... love to hear from many of his previous students.' This is a normal, reasonable request from a $4,000 buyer and there is no honest scripted response to it. The rep improvised three moves: authority ('I've had this conversation almost 2000 times'), a pre-emptive discount of any material he might send ('naturally, you're not going to put any bad results on our website'), and a claimed regulatory backstop that is not true — 'you're legally protected by the FTC to actually request a chargeback.' A one-page programme outline and a testimonial set would have cost nothing and were the actual answer. Flagged.

Triggered twice — 'I would just want to sit and think which program' and later 'I just also now need to sit and think if I want to really jump into a program like this.' Ran: the isolating probe ('why do you feel like you need that in order to make [a decision]?'), the do-it-to-know-it reframe ('the best way for you to understand if something's actually going to work is to actually do it'), and the $1,200 trial as a risk-reducer. Not run: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', and 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now' — which was the strongest available line given how much identity material Phase 3 had produced. The rep then stopped and disqualified rather than continuing, which was the right judgement even though it scores as an abandoned play.

A price reaction did land — 'transparently, I wasn't expecting it to be this high' — and none of the play ran: no isolation, no HOW-not-SHOULD frame, no permission question, no financial-picture questions. Recorded for completeness rather than as a criticism: the prospect neutralised his own objection in the same sentence ('but absolutely respect him and his price'), money was demonstrably not the blocker, and running the open-wallet sequence on an optimizer whose objection is scope would have been the wrong move. The isolation question alone would have been worth asking, because it would have surfaced the scope objection ten minutes earlier.

notes: Phases 3 and 4 are the best paired run in this folder — the bloodline and family-burden sequence is genuinely skilled discovery, and the self-sufficiency challenge produced insight rather than a concession for once. The call was lost between Phase 5 and Phase 6. Against a prospect who describes himself as comfortable and plateaued, the Consequence Frame was the whole job and it did not run; then a six-or-seven with a stated information deficit was answered with a different question and price was presented anyway. The single highest-value change: at 00:29:49 the prospect said exactly what he needed — more touchpoints and more visibility of the programme — and sending a one-page outline and a testimonial set would likely have closed this. Instead the request was reframed as avoidance and backed with a false claim about FTC protection, which is flagged. Credit where it is due: the disqualification was honest, the reasoning was sound, and the lower-tier onboarding was completed properly on the call.
